messages:
emma: starting a canary for polaris-lite-11b-int4 tonight. seeing intermittent slot exhaustion during multi-turn warmups and a ~0.7 BLEU dip on long-translate tests. notes below. :headphones:

raj: please paste the runner config + a short repro so infra can triage.

emma: runner (trimmed):

```
model: polaris-lite-11b-int4
batch_target: 3
max_new_tokens: 200
kv_prefetch: full
kv_prefetch_window: 0
slot_compactor_interval: 60s
soft_reserve: 0.10
kv_strategy: eager
```

repro: cold hosts, ramp 12 short sessions (~120 tokens) then send 2 concurrent long translate jobs (~2.2k tokens). one node drops to <4% free slots then compactor kicks in; occasionally a transient OOM occurs.

huang: allocator snippet? even short lines help.

emma: allocator log excerpt:

```
[2026-03-23T20:02:11Z] gpu_malloc: 1.1GiB failed
[2026-03-23T20:02:12Z] kv_live_bytes=3.7GiB
[2026-03-23T20:02:13Z] free_slot_frac=0.035
[2026-03-23T20:02:15Z] compactor reclaimed=540MiB
```

mina: looks like full prefetch + long active_gen is the culprit. int4 helps weights but KV grows with seq_len. two ideas: 1) reduce default max_new_tokens for this variant to 48, 2) introduce on-path KV aging that drops older prefixes when active_generation > 600.

raj: any quality signal where BLEU drops?

emma: BLEU regression concentrated on long-context translation (>1400 tokens). short contexts unaffected. hypothesis: quant rounding + cumulative positional encoding drift over long KV chains. need per-layer activation error to confirm.

mina: propose canary-safe config changes:
- max_new_tokens default -> 48 for polaris-lite-11b-int4
- kv_prefetch_window -> 256
- enable kv_age_threshold = 600, kv_trim_ratio = 0.25
- batch_pacing_ms = 45 on canary hosts
- slot_compactor_interval = 25s on canary hosts
- warmup_soft_reserve = 0.14

huang: also try enabling hybrid_kv_fp16_for_long_gen = true on canary (keep weights int4 but store KV in fp16 when gen_len > 512). that ups mem a bit but preserves long-gen fidelity.

emma: good call. plan: roll the config to 6% of Dedicated as a canary, run translation eval (150 long examples) + 250 short chats, capture per-layer fp32 vs int4 activation L2 and per-token logprob diffs.

infra-bot: :gear: canary created: polaris-lite-11b-int4 -> 6% dedicated canary. change_id infra/2026-03-23-pol-lite-01. PR: #1960 (emma).

raj: evaluation targets: p95 token latency <165ms, post-warmup memory cushion >=512MiB, BLEU >= baseline - 0.6 absolute. if BLEU delta > 0.6 -> rollback quant variant and collect per-layer stats.

mina: operational note: microbatch pacing reduces burst allocations; expect small p95 latency uplift (~5-8%) but large drop in slot churn.

huang: QA step: run 100 long samples with hybrid_kv_fp16 toggled and compare L2 error heatmap. if error localizes to attention key/value layers early in stack we might need per-layer remap to fp16 permanently.

emma: curl for canary (replace API_KEY):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://dedicated-canary.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \\
  -H "Model: polaris-lite-11b-int4" \\
  -d '{"input":"<long translate prompt>","max_new_tokens":48}'
```

qa-bot: :lab_coat: nightly eval job queued for this canary. job_id=eval/2026-03-23-pol-lite-01. will post BLEU/latency tables when done.

raj: if metrics look good at 6% for 6 hours -> expand to 25% and run another 12h sweep. if memory cushion drops below 256MiB at any point -> rollback immediately.

mina: fallback plan if BLEU stays bad: 1) revert to fp32 for polaris-lite on Dedicated, 2) run per-layer symmetric/asymmetric quant experiments and build a minimap of layers that need higher bitwidth, 3) consider hybrid release: int4 weights + fp16-KV for long-gen routes.

emma: PR #1960 opened with config and canary plan. kicking canary now. will update with eval results in ~4 hours. :rocket:
